body:
Setting:
I was at home, initially alone. After a while, a friend came over to smoke a joint with me but left later. Before, during, and after the trip I felt mentally stable and in a good mood.
Trip Report:
I started by taking a pack of DPH (about 1g) and did a medium-sized line of Ketamine. About an hour in, I felt a light DPH trip combined with some dissociation from the Ketamine. Then a friend called to ask if I wanted to smoke, so he came over.
A few hours later, the DPH started to kick in much harder. I took more Ketamine, and we listened to some speedcore and other fast music, which felt extremely slow and distorted. My coordination was noticeably affected but with enough focus I could still move around reasonably well.
Eventually, my friend had to leave. I stayed up, took more Ketamine, and tried to watch TV. My memory of this part is very fragmented, like everything was happening in slow motion but also like a slideshow where half the frames were missing.
At some point I called another friend, who told me to watch a specific movie on a TV channel. I apparently took five minutes just to find the right channel, constantly forgetting which one I was supposed to be looking for. He later told me I kept starting sentences and then stopping halfway through, and that I even forgot we were on the phone a few times.
After hanging up, I went to my room, took another line, and lay down in bed. Thats when things went into full dissociative delirium. I lost all sense of body and space. I began having thoughts that, looking back, I can't even begin to describe or understand. It felt like I was reaching the final frontier of thought itselfas if the entire universe existed only for the next thought, the ultimate realization
It felt like I was reaching the final frontier of thought itselfas if the entire universe existed only for the next thought, the ultimate realization
, but that thought was so alien to anything the human mind could grasp that I cant even come close to recalling or explaining it now.
Gradually, I came back down, sobered up a bit, and eventually fell asleep.
Aftermath:
I woke up the next morning feeling surprisingly fine. No muscle soreness, no real anticholinergic hangover, no bowel issues. My pulse stayed normal for most of the trip, with a maximum of 126 bpm. The only lingering effect was the occasional sensation of sudden, sharp movement in my head, but it wasnt unpleasant.
The main after-effect was that I kept thinking about that strange, unreachable thought I hadsomething I can neither fully remember nor comprehend, but which felt deeply significant in the moment.
